cells.date: Śaka 981 (chandra-sasa-graha), Vikāriṅ, Āshāḍha ba. 8, Monday=1050 A. D., July 5, Monday.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of a deserted village called Laghumōrambikā, situated in Gōpāla-dvīpa-vishaya, to Chhaṇḍama, chief of the king's bodyguards, evidently for populating it. The first 4 years and thirty-five months' revenue was fontly (free) for twenty years; and thirty-five Bhāramikas each month; no other levy was to be collected from him. Chhadama belonged to the Tūjiva race, and was the son of Madliamada and grandson of Aliyamma. Noticed in the Quarterly Journal of the Bharata Itihasa Samshodhaka Maṇḍala (Marathi), Poona, Vol. XXXI, No. 4, pp. 27 ff.

Pāṇḍya and his brother Vīra-Pāṇḍya were the last of them.

cells.date: 22nd year, Kaṭaka 27, Saturday, Sōdi. = 1111 A. D. The day of the month was 20 (July 25), Saturday; the 6th was 12. '73.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary and built in at places. Seems to record a gift of money for lamps for some purpose to the god, by Chēra-Udaiyan Vaḷḷāḷa Āna ... of Vaṇḍāḷai in Tirumaraiyūr included in Kuḷōttuṅgachōḷa-vaḷanādu, having assembled the Perumakkal of the brahmadeya village Ārūndigai-chaturvēdimangalam in the temple of the Tiru-kōyil-uḍaiyār, and they had to provide land for the deity for meeting the expenses of the sacred bath on the day of the day of ēkādaśi. Another fragment close to this and dated in the 32nd year of the king also mentions the same donor and seems to refer to a similar donation by him. Two more frag-mentary inscriptions are on stones built into the steps of this shrine.
